materials.content_note: AIQ Opening Bell, Vol 6, Issue 8, August 1997. Interview by David Vomund. Used for NO_TRADE / FAILURE_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE / stop-process context in the NR7 semantic completion. 'The worst thing you can do in terms of market timing is to buy in the middle of a trading range. Either buy new highs, or buy pullbacks...'; 'Most often, I'll get out if the market fails to do what I thought it would do'; 'If I try to guess a breakout, I'm wrong 90 percent of the time' (also stated in the 2004 article); failure example Eaton Corp.
materials.content_type: official interview (Linda Bradford Raschke; patterns: Holy Grail, Three-Day Unfilled Gap Reversal, Wolfe Wave; timing; stops)
materials.diversity_role: no-trade (middle of range); stop process ('most often, I'll get out if the market fails to do what I thought it would do'); impulse/thrust/range-expansion cue list; failure example (Eaton Corp); source context for the selected family's no-trade and stop-process fields

materials.canonical_title: The Discerning Trader: Linda Bradford Raschke
materials.content_note: Stocks & Commodities V.11:9 (360-366), 1993, interview by Thom Hartle. KEY material for the NR7 family: Figure 2 'A narrow range seven-day (NR7) in today's trading range is the narrowest trading range in the last seven days. The low volatility leads to a trend' (September Cocoa); 'A good example might be buying the breakout of an NR7 day, which stands for a narrow range seven-day pattern... going with the volatility in that case'; 'I use different measurements for the amount of contraction in the market... that tells me to switch to a breakout mode'; 'if you ever get a middle, or a good trend day... you should always carry that trade overnight because the odds are that you will get follow through the next day'; 'The last hour's action is very important to me. I want to see how a market's going to perform at the end of the day, and if I like how it acts at the end of the day I will continue to carry the trade.'
materials.content_type: official interview (Thom Hartle; NR7 breakout; prior-day levels; breakout vs swing mode; contraction measure)
materials.diversity_role: NR7 definition + breakout entry (cocoa commodity-futures example); contraction-measure umbrella ('that tells me to switch to a breakout mode'); three-day trend structure (carry a good trend day overnight); end-of-day handling ('The last hour's action is very important to me')

materials.canonical_title: Trading Style and Daily Market Regimen
materials.content_note: Active Trader, February 2004, interview by Mark Etzkorn (a day with Linda Raschke, Nov 2003). PRIMARY material for the selected family: 'A trend day opens on one end of its range and closes on the opposite end, has range expansion, and makes a steady pattern of higher highs and higher lows, or vice versa, throughout the day. In the index futures, there are two or three trend days a month'; trend-day precursors (significant range contraction 'such as an NR7 day, which is a bar with the narrowest range of the past seven bars'; large opening gap; approaching new 20-day highs/lows); trend-day confirmation (large opening 15-min bar attributed to Toby Crabel, with 'you can determine the threshold of significance yourself'; 'a significant increase in volume in the first 15 minutes relative to the past two weeks'; leadership IBM/MSFT/INTC/GE; 'trendiness between say, 10 and 10:30 or 10:45 a.m.'; 'trend in the market breadth - the difference between advancing issues and declining issues'); 'Something I'll almost always do the day after an NR7 day is bracket stops around the early morning range. When I tested this out about five years ago, it didn't matter whether you bracketed the first 45 minutes range or the first hour's range. If there's going to be a trend day, you're going to catch it'; 'I'm looking to hold that position until the end of the day, or add to the position during the day, or maybe hold part of it overnight'; 'If I try to guess a breakout, I'm wrong 90 percent of the time.'
materials.content_type: official interview (Mark Etzkorn; trend days; NR7 bracket; wide-range bar; session windows)
materials.diversity_role: PRIMARY material: NR7 day definition; trend-day definition; trend-day precursors; trend-day confirmation (15-min bar, volume, leadership, trendiness 10-10:30/10:45, breadth); day-after-NR7 early-morning-range bracket (45-min vs 1-hour variants); hold-to-end-of-day / add / hold-part-overnight; no-trade (breakout guess 90% wrong; flags volatility failure)

materials.content_note: Active Trader, August 2000, interview by Mark Etzkorn. Used for EXIT_OR_TARGET and management context: 'The minute the market gives back more than it should, you get out on the first reaction or pause'; 'I try to stay with a position as long as I can and take half off'; 'if the market reaches a price objective and you're really not sure if it's going to continue, you have to at least take half the position off'; 'Ninety percent of what I do is price-based. Indicators are just derivatives of price'; 'I use the TICKs like a momentum oscillator... The bottoms of sell-offs will be accompanied by negative TICK extremes, like -1,000' (NYSE TICK = NOT_OBSERVABLE_WITH_CURRENT_DATA).
materials.content_type: official interview (Mark Etzkorn; price-based trading; management; risk; execution)
materials.diversity_role: management/exit principles for held positions ('The minute the market gives back more than it should, you get out on the first reaction or pause'; 'you have to at least take half the position off'); three-pushes momentum; NYSE TICK used like a momentum oscillator (unavailable-input boundary); 'Ninety percent of what I do is price-based'

materials.content_note: Active Trader, March 2004, interview by Mark Etzkorn (follow-up). Used for context on the breadth/TICK unavailable-input boundary and multi-timeframe scope. Indicator checklist includes closing breadth (10-period SMA of NYSE advancers minus decliners) and TICK/TIKI highs and lows - both NOT owned by the Chinese-futures corpus.

materials.diversity_role: indicator checklist context; closing breadth (10-period SMA of NYSE advancers minus decliners) as an unavailable-input boundary; Holy Grail across time frames (timeframe-context); TICK/TIKI highs and lows (unavailable-input boundary)
